requirements.text: Stuff the paper into the cup.
requirements.source_phrase: Stuffing the paper into the cup

outcomes.description: Paper is stuffed into the cup.
outcomes.target: The paper is visibly placed inside the cup, with evidence that it has been stuffed into it rather than merely resting nearby or on its rim.
outcomes.reference: The requested edit is stated in the instruction: “Stuffing the paper into the cup”.

nodes.question: Comparing source and edited images, is there clear visual evidence that the source paper has been placed into the source cup, or that a portion is being inserted?
nodes.criteria: Pass only when the source paper and cup are identifiable and the edited image visibly shows the paper inside the cup or being inserted into its opening. Fail only when both objects and their relation are clear and the paper is visibly not being inserted or placed inside. Unknown when object identity, visibility, or the paper-to-cup relation is ambiguous; do not infer absence from missing evidence.
nodes.binding: Assess only progress on stuffing the source paper into the source cup, using the source image to identify those objects. Mere proximity, overlap, or contact with an apparent rim is not insertion. Unrelated edits do not count.

nodes.question: Given the source paper and cup, does the edited image show the paper substantially placed and visibly stuffed inside the cup, rather than merely entering, resting on the rim, or being held nearby?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the identifiable paper is visibly substantially inside the identifiable cup in a configuration evidencing that it has been stuffed into it. Fail if the objects and placement are clear and show only partial entry, rim contact, nearby placement, or no insertion. Unknown if identity, visibility, or extent cannot be determined.
nodes.binding: Inspect source and edited images independently, using s1 as context. Judge the requested extent of stuffing, not mere approach or any overlap; do not assume an ambiguous round object is the source cup.

nodes.question: Does the image provide enough evidence to determine whether the paper has been stuffed into the cup?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the image clearly resolves whether the paper is inside the cup and stuffed into it. Fail if the image clearly shows it is not stuffed into the cup. Unknown if visibility or ambiguity prevents a determination; retain this as unresolved rather than inferring completion or absence.
nodes.binding: Use only visible evidence of the paper’s placement relative to the cup; do not treat proximity or contact with the rim alone as proof of stuffing.

nodes.question: Does the image show the paper stuffed inside the cup?
nodes.criteria: Complete only when s1 passes and stuffing_extent passes, establishing identifiable paper substantially stuffed inside the source cup. Partial only when s1 passes, establishing actual insertion or placement progress, but stuffing_extent fails to establish the requested extent. Absent only when s1 fails on clear evidence that the identifiable paper is not being inserted or placed inside the identifiable cup, with no requested progress. Unknown when object identity, placement, or extent is ambiguous or necessary evidence is unresolved; do not convert uncertainty into absence. Unrelated edits do not count.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

response.content: {"accepted":false,"reason":"The support checks overlap and contradict one another on the requested extent. `s1` passes for either actual insertion or completed placement, while `stuffing_extent` treats partial entry as a failure; `s2` then asks whether the paper is stuffed and can fail on that same partial entry. The fulfillment rule says `s1` pass plus `stuffing_extent` fail is partial, but also requires `s1` to establish actual insertion or placement progress, which its pass criteria do not distinguish from completed placement. Thus the composition cannot reliably separate progress from completion or absence. Revise the support propositions and composition so partial insertion is evidenced as progress, while only clear non-insertion supports absence."}
